trades.headline: Turn Downs and Johnson into Trevor Lawrence, playing the best football of his career
trades.summary: Sends receiver and tight end surplus to a WR/QB-thin rival for a red-hot dual-threat starter at your weakest position.

give: Downs' 29% target share only opened up after Alec Pierce got hurt; Colts split targets with Tyler Warren, capping him as WR depth you don't need.
Johnson's role is easily replaced by Dalton Schultz, who has outproduced him the last two weeks as a top-5 fantasy tight end.
get: Lawrence leads the NFL in average depth of target (11.1 yards) and was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week entering Week 3.
Black has out-touched Christian McCaffrey 21-20 through two weeks in a real committee, giving him standalone flex value.
you: Lawrence becomes your starting QB, replacing Daniel Jones' 132 FantasyCalc value and -78 trend outright.
Dalton Schultz (687 value, +517 trend) steps into the starting TE spot Johnson vacates, so the position doesn't downgrade.
them: The Bedouin (1-1) are thin at WR and QB; adding Downs fills their receiver need in a lateral QB swap to Goff.
They're deep at TE already, so absorbing Johnson as WR/QB-thin depth costs them nothing on the bench.

risks: Lawrence completes just 35.3% of throws under pressure, a soft spot a good pass rush could exploit.
If Alec Pierce returns healthy in Indianapolis, Downs' target share (and the Colts' incentive to deal him) could shrink back down.

trades.headline: Sell high on a hot tight end, buy the NFL's passing-yardage leader Tyler Shough
trades.summary: Moves an underperforming Metcalf and a spiked Schultz to a QB-deep rebuilder for Shough and a rookie TE1 replacement.

give: Metcalf has 4 drops and 2 needless offensive pass interference calls on just 19 targets through two games.
Schultz is riding a TE5, 26-point week with Nico Collins out; moving him now cashes in that spike before touches normalize.
get: Shough leads the NFL with 662 passing yards through two weeks and delivered a go-ahead rushing touchdown against Baltimore.
Ferguson has claimed the Rams' TE1 job: 71.4% route share, 26.9% target share, and a TE8 finish last week.
you: Shough takes the QB slot outright from Daniel Jones, a clear upgrade at your thinnest position.
Ferguson fills the flex/TE spot Schultz vacates so the position isn't left empty.
them: Ben Hur Returns (0-2) are thin at TE and WR and deep at QB, so trading Shough away costs them a surplus piece.
Metcalf and Schultz fill two real holes for a rebuilding roster hunting difference-makers at receiver and tight end.

risks: Shough's production is heavily fourth-quarter-driven (350 of his yards there); a low-scoring week could look different.
Ferguson still shares some early-down snaps with Tyler Higbee, which can cap his floor in a given week.

trades.headline: Sell Diggs at his touchdown-fueled peak, buy a struggling Herbert before positive regression
trades.summary: Cashes in Diggs' hot start right as his QB situation downgrades, for a talented Herbert stuck in an 0-2 execution slump.

give: Diggs has 3 touchdowns on just 15 targets through two games, scoring pace well ahead of his 21.7% target share.
Washington just lost Jayden Daniels (elbow) to backup Marcus Mariota, a real downgrade to the QB play Diggs has been producing behind.
get: Both Chargers losses have come by the same 26-14 score with clear execution issues (drops, false starts) rather than a talent shortfall.
Herbert and OC Mike McDaniel are meeting more to fix a 28th-ranked scoring offense, a buy-low window before it turns.
you: Herbert takes over as your starting QB, replacing Daniel Jones' -78 trend outright.
You keep DK Metcalf and Josh Downs as receiver depth after moving only Diggs out of the flex spot.
them: ChampaignTornadoes (1-1) are deep at QB and WR but thin at RB and TE, and are still adding scoring punch at receiver.
Diggs' current touchdown pace makes him an appealing rental for a team already stacked at the position.

risks: Herbert has yet to complete a single pass of 20+ air yards this season, a sign the buy-low could be early.
Diggs may keep producing regardless of QB, since Washington's passing game now runs through him as the clear No. 2 option.
